body:
I’m 50 and based in London, UK, and I finally have my MIS bunion surgery scheduled for the end of this month. After consulting with two different surgeons, we agreed that MIS was the most suitable option for me.

My bunion is moderate rather than severe, my toe still has good mobility, and my soft tissue is healthy — all indicators that the deformity can be corrected safely through tiny incisions without the larger exposure required in open surgery.

Staying physically active is important to me, and my surgeon believes that gentle movement will play a key role in my recovery. I also feel confident knowing that my surgeon is highly experienced with this technique.

Social media can sometimes feel like a place where "polarised opinions" dominate, and I’m certainly not promoting this method over any other. Every case is individual.

But if you’re considering bunion surgery, speak directly with medical professionals, ask questions, and gather as much information as you can so you can make the decision that’s right for you.

body:
So I went to see a new podiatrist for a toenail injury and mentioned I’m recovering from 18 mos of plantar fasciitis. She sent me home with a list of treatments that I had NEVER heard from the 3 other podiatrists I’d seen (all of whom opted for invasive and expensive treatments) So far so good! Her list:

1.  Leg length discrepancy test. Basically an X-ray of both legs to see if they are slightly different lengths. She can fix this with a small orthotic lift. I have not had the X-ray yet. 

2. Heating pad to calf 10 min the rolling pin to calf 2 min. 

3. Compression socks (Amazon). Not too ugly. 

4. Nitro patch (prescription). Cut into ¼ piece and wear on heel 10-12 hours. 

5. NO heel raise exercises. (Shortens the calf muscle- who knew!) continue calf stretches. 

6. Continue ART and Graston. 

I am confident she knows what she’s doing and I’m also angry that I spent time, money, pain and energy on steroid injections, shockwave treatments, ointments, supplements, splints, boots, dry needling (thickens fascia!!!). 
But I do like my orthotics. 

Not saying this will work for everyone but my fasciitis was likely caused by shin splints and weak ankles. 

Better everyday!
